meta.question: Should we build or buy our CRM?
meta.title: CRM: build, buy or adapt open source
meta.author: Product and engineering leads, Brackenfield Events (fictional)
meta.footer: Fictional company and figures, for illustration only. Costs are three-year estimates in GBP.

answer.headline: Buy: a hosted CRM costs about £186k over three years against £540k to build, is live in three months instead of twelve, and our needs are standard. Build only the event-booking integration.
answer.text: We need contacts, deals, email tracking and reporting for 45 sales and account staff. Nothing in that list is unique to us; the one thing that is, the link to our event-booking system, is a small integration either way.
points: Three-year cost: buy £186k, adapt open source £310k, build £540k
Time to first users: buy 3 months, open source 6, build 12
The risk with buying is lock-in; we limit it by keeping our own nightly data export

options.name: Buy a hosted CRM
options.summary: Subscribe to a mainstream CRM and configure it.
pros: Upgrades, security and uptime are the vendor's job

options.name: Adapt an open-source CRM
options.summary: Host and extend an open-source CRM ourselves.
pros: Full control of data and code
cons: We run hosting, upgrades and security
Needs a developer most of the time

options.name: Build our own
options.summary: Write a CRM around our event model.
cons: Twelve months before anyone uses it
We own every bug and feature request for ever

blocks.title: Three-year cost by option
blocks.caption: Licences: 45 users at about £78 a month. Build and support at internal day rates.

blocks.title: How the options score against our needs
When building would be the right answer

items.title: The CRM is the product
items.text: If customers paid us for the way we manage relationships, owning it would be worth the cost.

items.title: Unusual data or rules
items.text: If no product could hold our data model without heavy workarounds.

items.title: Scale that breaks per-user pricing
items.text: Thousands of users can make licences dearer than a team of developers.
Two-week trial with five sales staff
Confirm a full data export in a standard format
Check data is stored in the UK or EU
Agree a price cap for renewal years two and three

blocks.label: Assumptions to check
blocks.body: Build cost assumes two developers for twelve months and one afterwards. If the trial shows we need heavy customisation, the gap between buy and open source narrows and the decision should be revisited.
